notes.purpose: Together these two files implement jaxfne's configuration layer: _runtime_config.py (314 lines) holds RuntimeConfig/SurrogateConfig -- the JAX runtime/dtype/device/backend policy plus homeostasis/HDP toggles used at simulate() time -- and _config.py (1492 lines) holds Configuration -- the frozen, purely-declarative TFNE model-declaration object (networks/emitters/fields/probes/metadata) built via a chainable fluent API. _config.py imports RuntimeConfig from _runtime_config.py (line 25) only to read its default homeostasis_params/hdp_params dicts when Configuration.homeostasis()/hdp() need to seed defaults (lines 599, 626) -- Configuration never constructs/consumes a compiled RuntimeConfig otherwise. Both were split out of the former jaxfne/core.py monolith (docs/v047_refactor_audit.md): _runtime_config.py first (commit ad87e85, "zero internal core.py dependencies"), then _config.py (commit 5a7e75d, "Configuration ... plus 5 group-1 helpers"), with core.py re-exporting everything from both for backward compatibility.

contracts: Import discipline: import Configuration/RuntimeConfig from jaxfne.core (or jaxfne.runtime for RuntimeConfig) per both module docstrings -- these files exist to be re-exported, not imported directly by feature code.

Configuration is a frozen dataclass (line 232); every chainable method returns a new instance via dataclasses.replace, never mutates self -- stated explicitly in the class docstring (lines 234-239) and module docstring ('purely declarative... do not touch dynamics').

update_metadata() is the only sanctioned path to merge metadata; it always routes through clamp_truth_gate_metadata() (line 334) so claim_level/field_claim_level/field_solver_status/physical_amplitude_calibrated cannot be escalated by a caller.

connections(...) (lines 667-757): mechanism resolution to real tau/receptor_index at construct() time only happens when EVERY declared rule has a resolvable mechanism= reference; one rule omitting mechanism= falls the whole config back to the sign-only heuristic (exc=2ms/inh=5ms), per docstring lines 696-704 and core._all_connection_rules_declare_resolvable_mechanism.

probe()/set_probes() reject the retired '*_like' probe vocabulary via _reject_retired_like (lines 158-171) -- e.g. 'lfp_like' raises ValueError directing callers to 'lfp_proxy'; no backward-compat alias exists.
RuntimeConfig.enable_homeostasis and enable_hdp are mutually exclusive (lines 102-106) -- setting both True raises ValueError at construction, verified by two independent tests.
RuntimeConfig.dtype/dtype_primary must be one of ('float32','float64','bfloat16') (_ALLOWED_DTYPES, line 19) or construction raises -- no silent fallback remains.

(lines 860-899): activation_rule/conductance_rule/homeostasis_rule are registry name strings only (validated at construct() time) because Configuration must stay JSON-safe for jaxfne.io.json_safe/config_hash -- a custom callable rule must call emitters_homeostatic_ei.simulate_homeostatic_ei directly instead.
landmines: Configuration.homeostasis()/hdp() (lines 578-630) instantiate a bare RuntimeConfig() purely to read its default homeostasis_params/hdp_params dict (lines 599, 626) every time either method is chained -- if RuntimeConfig's __post_init__ ever grows external-state dependence this becomes a surprising side effect inside a purely-declarative method.

_default_metadata's field_solver_status allow-list includes 'pde_solver' marked 'reserved token; amplitude still forced False' (line 94) -- even a nominally-real PDE solver status still hard-pins physical_amplitude_calibrated=False (line 126), so the token is a no-op today by design, not a real solver switch.

_ProbeDeclarations (lines 174-229) is a list subclass that is ALSO callable (cfg.probes([...])) -- naive reassignment of cfg.probes outside __post_init__'s owner-rebind check (lines 260-262) could silently detach the owner reference and raise TypeError only when called, not at assignment time.

RuntimeConfig.actual_dtype (lines 143-150) silently downgrades a requested float64 to float32 at read time if jax_enable_x64 is not globally enabled -- distinct from the hard dtype validation in __post_init__; a caller can request 'float64', pass validation, and still silently execute in float32 unless x64 was enabled process-wide first (classic jax-neuro-diffsim-guard x64-before-arrays landmine).

connections() only warns (UserWarning, not error) when mechanism= references an undeclared .mechanisms() name (lines 748-756) -- docstring explicitly flags this becomes a hard error in a future v0.3.30 compiler, so current warning-tolerant callers will break on a future version bump.

_config.py has 5 commits vs _runtime_config.py's 1 -- the runtime/dtype policy file has been stable since its single extraction commit, while _config.py keeps absorbing new declarative-DSL surface area (circuit/training declarations, Suite No.2/5 multi-area methods), making it the far larger, more actively-extended half of this pair despite the shared extraction origin.
